text:
## Escalation Matrix  
**Complaint Escalation by Severity & Involvement:**  
| Level | Authority | Timeline | Complaints |
|-------|-----------|----------|-----------|
| **Frontline** | Customer Service Agent | <1 day | Simple, low-value |
| **Manager** | Complaints Manager | <5 days | Moderate issues, <£500 loss |
| **Director** | Head of Customer Service | <8 days | Significant issues, >£500 loss |
| **Escalated** | CEO/Board | 8+ weeks | Major failures, reputational risk |  
**Escalation Triggers:**
- Complaint unresolved after manager review
- Financial compensation >£500
- Regulatory or reputational concern
- Media/legal involvement
- Customer escalates to FCA

properties.core_policy_statement: Establishment of a tiered escalation matrix based on severity, financial value, and involvement to ensure timely resolution of customer complaints.

properties.risk_definition: Risks associated with major failures or public perception

specific_obligations: Resolve simple, low-value complaints within 1 day
Resolve moderate issues with <£500 loss within 5 days
Resolve significant issues with >£500 loss within 8 days
Handle major failures and reputational risks within 8+ weeks

relationships.description: The policy is designed to meet the standards and requirements set by the FCA.
The policy provides a framework to manage and mitigate risks to the bank's reputation.
The policy defines the resolution timeline for frontline staff.
The policy defines the resolution timeline for managers.
The policy defines the resolution timeline for directors.
relationships.context: Director | Head of Customer Service | <8 days

relationships.description: The policy defines the resolution timeline for executive leadership.
The policy specifies the conditions that trigger a complaint escalation.
Frontline resolution timelines are the responsibility of the Customer Service Agent.
Manager resolution timelines are the responsibility of the Complaints Manager.
Director resolution timelines are the responsibility of the Head of Customer Service.
relationships.context: Director | Head of Customer Service | <8 days

relationships.description: Executive resolution timelines are the responsibility of the CEO and Board.
Reputational concerns act as a trigger for mandatory escalation.
Customer escalation to the FCA triggers a mandatory internal escalation.
Escalation triggers are based on the nature of the customer's complaint and actions.
Customer Service Agents escalate unresolved complaints to the Complaints Manager.
Complaints Managers escalate significant issues to the Head of Customer Service.
The Head of Customer Service escalates major failures to the CEO and Board.
The policy governs how complaining customers are handled through the escalation matrix.
